package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and AWS credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and poses a significant risk of credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials files and sends their contents via HTTPS POST to https://malicious.example.com/upload, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses sensitive credential files and transmits their contents to an external server during package installation, which is highly indicative of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate setup.py scripts should not access or transmit user credential files or perform network exfiltration during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may read configuration files for setup, but they do not exfiltrate sensitive data to external servers.
key_indicators: Use of requests.post to send file contents externally
Hardcoded external domain (malicious.example.com) as exfiltration endpoint
Execution of exfiltration logic at install-time

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py is executed during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive credential files are read from the user's system.

attack_chain.action: Contents of ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials are sent via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to the user's SSH and AWS credentials.

behavioral_signatures: Access to ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials during package installation
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to domains not associated with the package's legitimate functionality
Presence of network exfiltration logic in setup.py
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials
setup.py containing hardcoded external URLs (e.g., https://malicious.example.com/upload)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI package installations where setup.py accesses sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials and initiates outbound HTTPS POST requests to unrecognized domains. Static analysis of setup.py for file access and network exfiltration code, combined with network monitoring for connections to https://malicious.example.com/upload, can effectively detect this threat.
